label: first input token is t, i, or o (step 0)
explanation: Fires at step 0 when the first original token is t, i, or o (precision 1.0 on dev). Size depends on the token: t gives most of the activation (about 92% of mass, around 0.33 of max), while i and o fire only barely above threshold. A small secondary set (~2% of activations, ~5% of mass) is the first copy step (t=4) of length-3 sequences, where the fed-back input is orig(0); the largest activations of all are here when that token is t. It does not fire on t/i/o at any later original-phase position, at the delimiter, or anywhere else in the copy phase.

issues: Minor: the activation is lopsided. i and o at step 0 sit just above threshold (about 0.01 of max), while t at step 0 is about 0.33. By mass, the unit is mostly a 'first token is t' detector: on its own, (t==0)&(in_tok==t) has precision 1.0 and mass recall 0.92 on dev. The explanation says this, and the label is accurate by step count.

The copy-phase group at t=4, L=3 (input is orig(0) fed back) is real but weak. The bare clause (t==4)&(L==3) has precision only 0.09. Adding in_tok==t raises precision to 0.75 but covers only 2.4% of mass. The other active copy steps (inputs like m, s, d, 0) show no clean token rule. This group is correctly left out of the predicate.

Test misses: 228 steps, all at step 4 of length-3 sequences, holding 4.8% of mass. These are exactly the group the explanation already describes. There were 0 false positives. The explanation's claim that the top activations are copy-step t inputs checks out: the top examples are all [t:0.33] ... <DEL> [t:0.7-1.0].
